mature_ideas.title: Fission Neutron Release Timing as Discriminant for Transuranic r-Process Contributions
mature_ideas.hypothesis: The temporal profile of fission neutron release relative to (n,gamma)-(gamma,n) freeze-out produces a distinct signature in third r-process peak positioning that can discriminate fission-driven nucleosynthesis from alternative branching scenarios
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: The temporal profile of fission neutron release relative to (n,gamma)-(gamma,n) freeze-out produces a distinct signature in third r-process peak positioning that can discriminate fission-driven nucleosynthesis from alternative branching scenarios
mature_ideas.scientific_object: r-process abundance patterns with A > 250 fission fragments
mature_ideas.mechanism: Fission of transuranic nuclei (A > 260) releases neutrons at timescales determined by beta-decay chains; if release occurs before freeze-out, recycled neutrons shift the third peak position predictably; if after, peak remains unshifted
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Fission of transuranic nuclei (A > 260) releases neutrons at timescales determined by beta-decay chains; if release occurs before freeze-out, recycled neutrons shift the third peak position predictably; if after, peak remains unshifted
assumptions: Beta-decay rates for A > 250 nuclei follow systematic trends within theoretical uncertainty bounds
Fission fragment distributions are approximately model-independent for dominant cycling nuclei
Kilonova ejecta conditions permit multiple fission cycling episodes
evidence_basis: SURVEY_ANCHOR: The precise temporal relationship between fission neutron release and the freeze-out of neutron-capture equilibrium determines third-peak positioning, yet current network calculations lack constrained beta-decay rates far from stability to quantify this shift
mature_ideas.refinement_scope: Establish formal relation between fission neutron release timescale and third-peak shift magnitude; identify observable discriminants
mature_ideas.falsifier: Third-peak position shows no correlation with fission cycling conditions across nuclear model variations
mature_ideas.lineage: Derived from gap:sh2:mechanism_explanation_gap:fission_neutron_release_timing identifying missing temporal constraint on fission neutron release

mature_ideas.title: Continuous Density-Dependent Network Coupling for r-Process Calculations
mature_ideas.hypothesis: Replacing the artificial fixed-density threshold for switching from equilibrium to dynamical r-process with a continuous opacity-weighted coupling eliminates discontinuity errors in abundance predictions
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: Replacing the artificial fixed-density threshold for switching from equilibrium to dynamical r-process with a continuous opacity-weighted coupling eliminates discontinuity errors in abundance predictions
mature_ideas.mechanism: Network equations transition smoothly from NSE/statistical equilibrium to full dynamical tracking via density- and temperature-dependent weighting functions that preserve mass and energy conservation across the transition region
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Network equations transition smoothly from NSE/statistical equilibrium to full dynamical tracking via density- and temperature-dependent weighting functions that preserve mass and energy conservation across the transition region
assumptions: Equilibrium and dynamical network solutions converge in overlapping validity regime
Conservation laws hold across transition region
evidence_basis: SURVEY_ANCHOR: The switch from equilibrium to dynamical r-process calculations occurs at a fixed density threshold (~4 x 10^11 g cm^-3), introducing an artificial discontinuity that may propagate errors into final abundance predictions
mature_ideas.refinement_scope: Formulate continuous coupling scheme; quantify error reduction vs. fixed-threshold approach
mature_ideas.falsifier: Continuous coupling introduces larger errors than fixed threshold due to numerical stiffness
